title: Deny producer edits to unlisted governance files during the run
summary: The producer's PreToolUse policy gains a protected-path list: governance files the accepted reading does not both list as a deliverable and name in a criterion. Edit/Write (and Bash redirects) to those paths are denied at once with the "stop and report in open_issues" instruction. Admission's after-the-fact check stays as the backstop. Audience: Athena operators and the producer agent.

defaults_applied.how: Rule enforced by the PreToolUse hook rather than prompt text alone.
Unit tests for the policy and policy construction; cargo test and clippy clean.
Fixes the late check by moving enforcement into the work loop, not just these two files.
Criteria check denials actually occur by running the tests.
One focused change to the policy and its wiring.
Docs and changelog explain the new behavior.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Chose the enforcement option (deny at edit time through the existing PreToolUse hook) over making the reader list the file, because the reader cannot know what the producer will need and the user's goal is that refusal comes before the work.
The producer's own stop-and-report rule in producer.md exists but was not obeyed, so a mechanism is needed (mechanism default).
Cargo.toml lints-table edits cannot be denied by whole-file path, so they stay admission-only; this is documented, not solved.
The accepted reading is available when the producer's agent_spec is built (run.rs builds AcceptedReading with is_governance before the producer runs).

acceptance_criteria.text: A new unit test in crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs shows evaluate() returns Deny for Edit and Write on a path in the policy's protected list (e.g. athena.toml, .github/workflows/ci.yml), with a reason telling the producer to stop and report in open_issues, and NoObjection for an unprotected path. Run: cargo test -p athena-agent.

A unit test shows a Bash output redirect (e.g. `echo x > athena.toml`) to a protected path is denied, and that a protected path reached via `..` or a symlink inside the snapshot is still denied. Run: cargo test -p athena-agent.

A test in athena-core shows the producer's written policy file protects exactly the governance files (per is_governance) that the accepted reading does not both list as a deliverable and name in an acceptance criterion; a listed-and-named governance file is not protected, and non-producer roles are unaffected. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
An older policy JSON without the protected field still deserializes (serde default empty), and cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets, and cargo fmt --check pass across the workspace.

The producer prompt (crates/athena-context/prompts/producer.md) and the policy module docs state that the hook now enforces the governance rule at edit time, and that admission remains the backstop; docs/enforcement.md and CHANGELOG.md record the change, including that Cargo.toml lints-table edits are still caught only at admission.
No governance file (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, rust-toolchain.toml) is changed by this job.

out_of_scope: Changing admission's final governance check or its rules
Enforcing the Cargo.toml lints-table rule at edit time
Changing reader behavior or deliverable-listing heuristics
Recovering the two lost jobs 3htd and ksq0
departures: Touches the policy struct, the hook, and run wiring plus tests, so somewhat above the reference median cost and time.
